COMPLETE GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

Create a complete, standalone, highly realistic 3D aviation disaster simulation sandbox. The game must combine advanced aircraft simulation, realistic crash physics, dynamic destruction, passenger simulation, emergency rescue operations, black box investigation, cinematic replays, witness recordings, and a massive procedural world generator.

This is a serious, detailed simulation game, not an arcade flying game.

IMPORTANT REQUIREMENTS:

- Do not use Roblox or mention Roblox anywhere.
- Do not include any donations, microtransactions, subscriptions, paid content, premium features, or pay-to-win mechanics.
- All game features must be available without additional payments.
- Create a complete playable game, not just a visual prototype.
- All aircraft, buildings, environments, NPCs, and vehicles must use detailed 3D models.
- Avoid primitive-looking geometric placeholder models.
- Prioritize realistic physics and believable interactions.
- Support mobile touchscreen controls and PC controls.
- Make the game visually impressive while maintaining good performance.

1. MAIN GAMEPLAY — FREE CAMERA SANDBOX

The main game mode is a completely free 3D simulation sandbox.

When entering the world, the player starts in Free Camera mode.

The player can freely fly around the entire map, inspect buildings, explore the environment, and observe aircraft.

Add a prominent SPAWN AIRCRAFT button.

When pressed, open a detailed aircraft selection interface.

The player can select an aircraft, spawn it anywhere on the map, and configure its initial conditions.

Aircraft placement options:

- Position.
- Altitude.
- Direction.
- Starting speed.
- Aircraft condition.
- Engine condition.
- Landing gear condition.
- Passenger count.
- Weather conditions.

After spawning, the aircraft becomes a fully simulated physical object.

The player can spawn multiple aircraft simultaneously and observe interactions between them.

Add object selection. When selecting an aircraft, show its name, condition, components, and available actions.

2. AIRCRAFT LIBRARY

Create a large aircraft collection.

Include:

- Boeing 737.
- Boeing 747.
- Boeing 777.
- Boeing 787.
- Airbus A320.
- Airbus A330.
- Airbus A350.
- Airbus A380.
- Embraer regional aircraft.
- ATR turboprop aircraft.
- Cargo aircraft.
- Military transport aircraft.
- Passenger helicopters.
- Military helicopters.
- Fighter aircraft.

Every aircraft must have a unique, detailed exterior model and recognizable proportions.

Aircraft interiors should include:

- Cockpit.
- Pilot seats.
- Instrument panels.
- Passenger cabin.
- Passenger seats.
- Overhead compartments.
- Windows.
- Emergency exits.
- Cargo areas where applicable.

Do not use one generic aircraft model with different names.

3. ADVANCED AIRCRAFT PHYSICS

Implement a sophisticated physics simulation.

Every aircraft must have its own physical characteristics.

Simulate:

- Weight and center of mass.
- Aerodynamic lift.
- Air resistance.
- Gravity.
- Inertia.
- Wind influence.
- Turbulence.
- Aircraft stability.
- Engine thrust.
- Control surfaces.
- Landing gear.
- Ground friction.
- Water interaction.

Aircraft must behave differently depending on their construction and physical properties.

Damage must affect aircraft performance dynamically.

For example, a damaged wing should influence aircraft stability, while engine failure should affect thrust.

Aircraft must not fly along fixed animations. Their movements must be calculated through the simulation.

4. REALISTIC DAMAGE AND DESTRUCTION SYSTEM

Create a detailed component-based damage system.

Every aircraft must contain independently damageable parts.

Components include:

- Nose.
- Cockpit.
- Fuselage.
- Left wing.
- Right wing.
- Tail.
- Vertical stabilizer.
- Horizontal stabilizers.
- Engines.
- Landing gear.
- Doors.
- Windows.

This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D aviation incident simulation sandbox with a free camera, aircraft selection and spawning, physics, damage, rescue operations, replays, and flight-recording features.

## Requirements
- Standalone browser game; no donations, microtransactions, subscriptions, or paid mechanics.
- Detailed 3D models for aircraft, environment, vehicles, and structures, rather than primitive placeholder geometry.
- Realistic enough aircraft physics and component-based damage with crash and rescue interactions.
- Support PC and mobile touchscreen controls.
- Maintain attractive visuals and reasonable performance.
- Include multiple recognizable aircraft types with distinct proportions.
- No mention or use of prohibited platform terminology.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a static Three.js browser application using procedural geometry.
- Used a polished dark flight-operations interface over a coastal procedural 3D environment.
- Started with a live demo A320-class aircraft in the world.
- Included multiple aircraft variants: Airbus A320, Boeing 737-800, Boeing 747-400, and Embraer E175.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the primary HTML game shell and flight-operations interface.
- Created the responsive desktop/mobile CSS design.
- Created the Three.js scene foundation, lighting, fog, terrain, water, city, airport, runway, terminal, roads, and tree environment.
- Added detailed procedural aircraft geometry with distinctive fuselages, wings, tail components, engines, cockpit glazing, windows, doors, landing gear, and navigation lights.
- Added fleet selection and aircraft spawning configuration.
- Added free-camera orbit, zoom, keyboard movement, and mobile touch support.
- Added aircraft selection, object inspector, telemetry, active-aircraft list, and inspector actions.
- Added basic flight simulation, wind, lift/drag behavior, engine condition, structural damage, ground contacts, impacts, rescue vehicles, weather cycles, cinematic replay, and recorder events.

### Active
- No explicit active work recorded; implementation is in progress and not verified end-to-end.

### Blocked
- The app needs validation that the browser module and the final JavaScript file load correctly without syntax/runtime errors.
- The very large implementation file was edited and has likely had partial overwrite activity, so a clean, complete final `app.js` must be verified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html`, `style.css`, and `app.js` to verify that `app.js` contains the full implementation and has no truncation or duplicate/conflicting code.
2. Run the game through a local static server.
3. Verify Three.js loads and that the scene renders without console errors.
4. Test aircraft spawning, selection, camera controls, weather changes, damage, rescue dispatch, replay, and mobile responsiveness.
5. Capture a viewport screenshot and inspect it for visual completeness.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main game interface and modals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: Desktop/mobile simulator presentation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js`: Three.js scene, aircraft, physics, damage, UI, and interaction implementation.

## Important Context
- The implementation uses Three.js from a CDN module URL.
- The environment may require SwiftShader/CPU software rendering rather than hardware WebGPU.
- The current requested scope was much larger than the implemented MVP; many aircraft listed by the original prompt are not yet implemented.
- Potentially more complete/concatenated implementation state may exist in prior shell/edit history, but the final file must be examined before building.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D aviation incident simulation sandbox as a standalone browser game.

## Requirements
- No donations, microtransactions, subscriptions, or paid mechanics.
- Detailed aircraft, environment, vehicles, and structures; realistic flight physics, component damage, crashes, and rescue interactions.
- Free camera, aircraft selection/spawning, replays, flight recording, and PC/mobile controls.
- Attractive visuals, reasonable performance, and recognizable aircraft with distinct proportions.

## Decisions
- Use a static Three.js browser app with procedural geometry and a coastal flight-operations interface.
- Include Airbus A320, Boeing 737-800, Boeing 747-400, and Embraer E175; begin with a live A320-class aircraft.
- Start focused on and tracking the seeded aircraft so it is easier to see immediately.
- Use pointer events for orbit controls to support touch input on mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game interface, procedural coastal airport environment, and four distinct aircraft models.
- Implemented spawning, selection, camera/input handling, simulation, rescue, weather, replay, and recorder functionality.
- Set initial selection and camera focus to the seeded aircraft; adjusted it to start near the runway.
- Updated pointer orbit handling for touch devices.
- `node --check app.js` passes; Chromium rendered desktop and mobile captures.

- End-to-end gameplay interactions have not been verified in-browser; captures confirm rendering, not full interaction correctness.

2. Review mobile layout and test touch orbit and controls.
3. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main interface and dialogs.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile simulator styling.
- `app.js`: Three.js scene, aircraft, simulation, and interaction logic.
- `app-tail.js`: Retained separate source containing appended simulation/recovery implementation.
